grammar: tree-sitter-scss@1.0.0 (vendored, 2 local patches) — wasm wasm/tree-sitter-scss.wasm, sha256 729731fb83e4…, 195 ids / 84 named / 7 fields

inherits.reason: The SCSS grammar is `grammar(require('tree-sitter-css/grammar'), {…})` — a SUPERSET. Every CSS ruling applies here through the delegated walk in RealCssAnalyzer, and this spec deliberately does NOT restate them: 60 duplicated rulings would rot the moment either grammar moved and nobody would notice which half had gone stale.

each_statement.note: as `if_statement`, plus `scssEachKey`/`scssEachValue` read from the `key`/`value` FIELDS — the only place a stylesheet says what it is iterating.

extend_statement.note: a `uses` edge to the extended selector, named from the `class_selector`/`id_selector`/`plain_value` node's own text so the edge names the same symbol the file publishes.

forward_statement.note: as `use_statement`, minus the namespace (Sass's `@forward … as ns` names a prefix, not a binding). Also grammar patch 1/2.

function_statement.note: as `mixin_statement`, plus `scssReturns` when its body contains a `@return`. Pinned by scss/functions-return-and-undeclared-uses.

if_statement.note: an `interface` symbol named from the construct's own collapsed text, with `scssCondition`. The same shape the CSS lane gives `@supports`, and for the same reason: a CONDITIONAL SCOPE, not a declaration of a callable.

include_statement.note: a `uses` edge to a mixin THIS FILE declares, with the namespace resolved when the include is dotted (`map.get($k)`). Deliberately emits nothing for an undeclared mixin; pinned by a forbidRelationships row.

mixin_statement.note: publishes a `function` symbol named `@mixin <name>` with real `parameters` read from the `parameter` nodes and `defaultValue` from the `default` FIELD. Observed emitting across the corpus; pinned by scss/module-system-and-mixins and mutated by scss/callable-parameters-dropped.

plain_value.note: carries the value of a declaration, a mixin argument, and an `@extend` target when the target is an ELEMENT selector (`@extend p`) — there is no `type_selector` node in this grammar, which the analyzer's first case list wrongly named.

return_statement.note: recorded as `scssReturns` on the enclosing function — NOT as an edge. The first implementation emitted `contains` from the function to ITSELF, a self-edge that makes a relationship count look like evidence while connecting nothing. Mutated by scss/return-self-edge.

string_value.note: the module path of an `@use`/`@forward`, and a `@mixin`/`@function` name written in quotes.

use_statement.note: an `imports` edge plus an ImportInfo carrying the `as` namespace, and a `namespace` symbol for the bound name. The construct is GRAMMAR PATCH 1/2 — the stock rule was `seq('@use', $._value, ';')` and the `as` clause was the largest residual class in the corpus at 277 error spans.

variable.note: an ASSIGNMENT publishes a `variable` symbol, deduplicated by NAME across reassignments — a Sass variable is assigned in several places by design. A READ publishes a `references` edge, and only for a variable this file declares. Measured 223/223 of this lane's own `references` edges resolve at both ends.

while_statement.note: as `if_statement`. ZERO corpus occurrences — recorded as handled on the strength of a reproduction, which is a different claim from a corpus observation and is labelled as one.

call_expression.note: a `@function` CALLED in a value (`width: double(4px)`), which is the same class of claim as a `$var` read and was silently unreached until the M12 independent hand audit of validation/m12/fixtures/scss/Theme.scss reported it MISSING (9 expected, 8 observed, recall 0.889). The call's NAME is the part that decides whether a call is real, and a name is looked up in what the file DECLARES: builtins (`calc`, `var`, `rgba`, `min`, `url`) are not referents and produce no edge, which is the both-ends-resolve rule and the reason this type is reached rather than always-fired.

function_name.note: the CALLED name inside a `call_expression`. Reached only to decide whether a call resolves; a name this file does not declare as a `@function` is walked past, because the alternative is an edge to every CSS builtin in every stylesheet.

ERROR.note: tree-sitter's own recovery node, not a grammar type. The SCSS lane's `error-recovery-is-reported` fixture pins that a file the grammar cannot read still REPORTS the failure — measured 11 errors for two named `@page` at-rules, pinned at `atLeast: 1` so the number cannot break when the grammar improves.

MISSING.note: tree-sitter's own recovery node, not a grammar type. The SCSS lane's `error-recovery-is-reported` fixture pins that a file the grammar cannot read still REPORTS the failure — measured 11 errors for two named `@page` at-rules, pinned at `atLeast: 1` so the number cannot break when the grammar improves.

limitations.construct: the residual parse classes the grammar cannot represent
limitations.measured: 95 of 244 non-empty .scss files still fail. The residual is a LONG TAIL — largest class 24 error spans, most under 20 — against a single 277-span class before patch 1/2. The largest coherent group left is a namespaced function call, `map.merge($a, $b)`, at 12 spans.

limitations.construct: `@forward 'x' as prefix-*;` — the PREFIX form of the `as` clause
limitations.measured: 0 occurrences in 40,521 lines of corpus, where 359 uses are `as *` and 1 is `as common`. Supporting it needs `repeat1(seq('-', …))` after the name, which tree-sitter reports as an unresolved conflict with `binary_expression`. Carried in the A/B as `forward-as-dashed-prefix` with verdict `unchanged-broken`.

0 occurrences. The 33 interpolations followed by anything are inside names and strings (`#{$prefix}body-bg`). A fixture that pinned this form was written and then CORRECTED, because a fixture is supposed to pin constructs that exist.

limitations.construct: a map literal in an `@each` list — `@each $k, $v in (a: 1)`
limitations.measured: 0 occurrences. `@each $k in (a, b)` parses. Pinned by `error-recovery-is-reported` at `atLeast: 1` so the failure stays visible rather than silent.

limitations.construct: `@extend` of an id, a placeholder, a comma list, or a pseudo-class
limitations.measured: 5 `@extend` in 40,521 lines: 1 targets an `#id` and ERRORS, 4 target a `%placeholder` and ERROR. 0 use a comma list, 0 use a pseudo-class. The placeholder case is the more interesting half: `%ph { … }` PARSES and publishes `class:%ph`, so the declaration is understood and the `@extend` of it is not — a rule that is addressable but not extendable. Declared rather than patched on 5 occurrences.

limitations.construct: delegated CSS `var()` reads of externally-provided custom properties
limitations.measured: 14 of 220 resolve (6%) in the element-plus corpus, which consumes Element Plus theme tokens defined in another file. The behaviour is the CSS lane's own — verified by running identical input through both lanes — and this lane's own `$var` reads are 223/223 = 100%.

limitations.note: A `@function` call is resolved ONLY against functions the same file declares. A call into a module (`@use 'tokens' as t` then `t.$brand`, or a function defined in another partial) has no local declaration to resolve against, so it publishes no edge — the same no-phantom rule that keeps an undeclared `$var` or `@include` silent. Cross-file call resolution is not implemented and is not claimed: on element-plus the full-extent floor stands at MISSING 60 / unexplained 4.

RESOLVED 2026-09-29 by grammar patches 4 and 5, after three earlier attempts were measured and REVERTED. The entry stays because the attempts are the most useful part of it. PATCH 4 (maps) extends TWO EXISTING RULES rather than adding a third: `list_value` also accepts a keyed entry `KEY ':' VALUE`, and the inherited CSS `parenthesized_value` is widened from `'(' $._value ')'` to also accept `'(' $._value ':' $._value ')'`. The single-pair case is why the gap looked arbitrary — it lost to `parenthesized_value` while two-or-more pairs parsed, because a comma settles the conflict before precedence is consulted, and `prec.dynamic` cannot help because the conflict is resolved when the parser is GENERATED. The three REVERTED attempts all added a NEW `map_value` rule: in `_value` at prec 1 it fixed 5 files and regressed none while driving ERROR nodes 3,900 -> 8,056; scoped to call arguments it fixed 4 and REGRESSED 9; with `prec.dynamic` it was worse. A new rule competes in every declaration, selector and interpolation in the language, and where it loses tree-sitter recovers with an error node — which is why the file-level A/B reported '0 regressed' on a change that made the lane's worst files much worse. PATCH 5 (`@include` whitespace) relaxes only the CLOSING delimiter: the rule used `token.immediate` on BOTH parens, and `token.immediate` means zero intervening whitespace, so `@include f( 1px );` failed on a single space and the multi-line form — a design-system stylesheet's house style — failed too. MEASURED, cumulatively over the 244-file corpus: clean 149 -> 164 (61.1% -> 67.2%), 15 files fixed, 0 regressed, ERROR nodes 3,900 -> 3,089 (-21%). 10 of 12 hand-built map cases now parse, including the `map.merge` shape the corpus actually uses. The differential floor moved only 58 -> 58 with unexplained 4 -> 3, which is worth stating plainly: a large parse improvement is not automatically a graph improvement.

A NAMED ARGUMENT in a call — `color.channel($u, 'red', $space: rgb)` — does not parse. The `arguments` rule inherited from CSS is `token.immediate('(') sep(choice(',', ';'), repeat1($._value)) ')'`, bare values only, so the declaration is an ERROR. It is a strange one to lead the list because the lane ALREADY handles the identical shape for `@include`: `_include_argument` is `optional(seq(field('name', $.variable), ':')) field('value', $._value)`, written for exactly this. So the construct was understood by the grammar in one position and not the other — a gap, not a limitation. ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED 2026-09-29, and the reason is the part worth keeping. A patch was written, built and measured: 8 of 8 hand-built named-argument forms parsed (including the corpus shape), over the 244-file corpus it fixed 1 file, regressed 0, and removed 15 error nodes. The differential did not move AT ALL — 1614/1558, MISSING 56, unexplained 3, identical to four decimal places. So the patch's entire measured value was parse-level, and it was reverted because of what it COST rather than what it gained. It removes the only minimal construct on which the `scssRecoveredFromError` marker fires: a multi-line `$red: color.channel($upper, 'red', $space: rgb) * $opacity +` leaves the read INSIDE an ERROR subtree, while every still-broken alternative was tested and none fires the marker — the `@each` map-literal shape produces the same relationships with and without either descend-through-error walk, so it exercises nothing. Shipping the patch would have left the recovery machinery (229 recovered reads across 21 files corpus-wide) with no fixture at all, and `error-recovery-marker-dropped` would SURVIVE. A surviving mutant is a gate that cannot fail, which is the failure class this lane has spent the round eliminating. The fix shape is recorded and known: override `arguments` to admit `variable ':' value`. It must be ONE rule admitting both shapes, not `choice(original, …)` — the two-alternative form is rejected by `tree-sitter generate` as a genuine ambiguity with the inherited rule, not a parser limitation. Whoever takes this should expect to rebuild the recovery fixture on a construct that is declared-unsupported rather than merely unpatched.

RECOVERY IS STATEMENT-SCOPED, which bounds what error recovery can reach. The read/call scan is invoked for `declaration`, `include_statement`, control-flow and `return_statement` nodes, so a region where the STATEMENT ITSELF was destroyed by the grammar has nothing to hand the scanner and its reads stay invisible even though the walk descends through the error. Measured on `--font-size: #{map.get($input-font-size, $size)}` from `form-item.scss`: 15 error spans and ZERO relationships, where the same read recovered cleanly when the statement node survived. So recovery works where a statement node survives a parse failure and does not where the statement was destroyed. Corpus-wide the descend-through-error walks are worth 229 recovered `variable` reads across 21 files, 5 marked edges, and 4 symbols in `tag.scss` (scope-disambiguated `@each` interfaces and one variable) — real, but the outer walk in particular contributes 0 relationships and has no fixture, which is recorded here rather than left for a reader to assume.

corpusUnexercised.from: EMITTED, but not exercised by the corpus THIS lane's row is measured on — the shape `make` declared for its own `overrides`. (1) THE ZERO, over the whole corpus rather than a stride: `BB_PICK_CAP=1000 NFILES=400 bun script/m14/firing-check.mjs SCSS` reports 179/179 parsed of 179 admitted, corpus=bulma WHOLE, and `overrides` produces nothing there. There is no site for it to be rejected at either — bulma contains 0 occurrences of the substring `!global`, and a `!global` assignment is the only reassignment this lane emits `overrides` for, so a text search is sound for a ZERO here for the same reason CSS-D14 gives for `@import`. (2) THE EMISSION, so this is a corpus fact and not a capability gap: validation/m14/fixtures/scss/scss-relationship-census.ts records `overrides` 32 edges over 4433 admitted .scss files, identical in all five of the runs its header tabulates (which is what a type that does not move with the flaky-file set looks like), and the width of the class is pinned by validation/m14/fixtures/scss/module-exports-and-global-overrides.expectation.json, which EXPECTS the one honest edge (@mixin probe -> $brand, meta.overridesLine 4) and FORBIDS the three wide readings: $computed (a @function result is not an override), $invented (a `!global` that CREATES a global replaces nothing) and source $brand (an assignment overriding itself). Declared corpusUnexercised rather than implemented because the corpus this row is read from never exercises it.

coverage._extends_vs_css: SCSS and CSS do NOT disagree about `extends`, and the difference a reader will notice is explained by the GRAMMAR rather than by the ruling: the .css population cannot contain the construct at all — CSS-D14 counts 0 `@extend` at-rules and 0 candidate node types, so the CSS lane declares it grammar-absence — whereas tree-sitter-scss is `grammar(require('tree-sitter-css/grammar'), {…})` with an `extend_statement` production ADDED to that CSS base — `extend_statement: $ => seq('@extend', choice($._value, $.class_selector), ';')`, a plain rule of the vendored grammar and NOT one of its local patches, grammars/tree-sitter-scss/grammar.js:314 — so `@extend` is real syntax in this language and the type FIRES — 52 edges over the whole 179-file corpus, 38 on the committed 120-file stride, and this lane's `extend_statement` row in handled_verified above records how the target is named. `extends` is the ONE type whose verdict differs between the two lanes, and it differs because their grammars do.
